subject: Pathology
vignette: A 38-year-old woman has a 2 cm well-circumscribed, encapsulated mass in the uterine wall. Histology shows interlacing bundles of bland smooth muscle cells with very few mitoses, no necrosis, and no invasion of surrounding tissue.
question: Which of the following sets of features best distinguishes this benign leiomyoma from a leiomyosarcoma?

options.text: Rapid erratic growth, local invasion, and distant metastasis
Well differentiation, low mitotic activity, no invasion, no metastasis
Poor differentiation, high mitotic activity, and tumor necrosis
Nuclear pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and aneuploidy on cytology
Reactivation of telomerase with telomere elongation and immortalization

explanation_correct: Benign tumors are typically well differentiated and well demarcated, with low mitotic activity, no metastases, and no necrosis. Malignant tumors show poor differentiation, erratic growth, local invasion, metastasis, and decreased apoptosis. The described lesion fits the benign profile exactly: bland smooth muscle, rare mitoses, an intact capsule, and no necrosis.

explanation_incorrect.A: Rapid growth, invasion, and metastasis are the defining features of malignancy, which is the opposite of this circumscribed lesion.
explanation_incorrect.C: Poor differentiation with numerous mitoses and tumor necrosis are features of leiomyosarcoma, not of this bland encapsulated tumor.
explanation_incorrect.D: Marked pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and aneuploidy are malignant nuclear features and would argue against a benign leiomyoma.
explanation_incorrect.E: Telomerase reactivation supports limitless replicative potential and is a hallmark of cancer rather than a benign distinguishing feature.

educationalObjective: Benign = well differentiated, well demarcated, low mitoses, no invasion, no metastasis, no necrosis.
source: Generated from 4. Pathology.pdf - Neoplasia: Benign vs malignant characteristics

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 66-year-old man with a 30 pack-year smoking history has a 4 cm lung mass. The tumor shows marked nuclear pleomorphism with a high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, frequent mitoses, and extensive central necrosis.
question: Which of the following features would most firmly establish that this tumor is malignant rather than benign?

options.text: Metastasis to a distant organ
Increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio on cytology
Presence of a fibrous capsule around the mass
Cellular pleomorphism with variation in cell size
Elevated mitotic count on a single high-power field

explanation_correct: Metastasis is the single feature that unequivocally defines malignancy, because no benign tumor metastasizes. Many malignant features overlap with reactive or atypical benign processes: pleomorphism, increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, mitoses, and even necrosis can be seen in benign and premalignant lesions. Distant spread to a non-contiguous organ therefore settles the diagnosis.

explanation_incorrect.B: An increased nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio is a dysplastic feature and can be seen in reversible dysplasia and in reactive atypia, so it does not by itself prove malignancy.
explanation_incorrect.C: A capsule indicates circumscription and is characteristic of benign, well-demarcated tumors rather than of invasive cancers.
explanation_incorrect.D: Pleomorphism and variation in cell size describe dysplasia, which is often reversible and may accompany benign reactive change.
explanation_incorrect.E: A high mitotic count supports malignancy but also occurs in benign proliferations and in normal regenerative tissue, so it is not decisive alone.

educationalObjective: Metastasis is the defining, unambiguous criterion of malignancy; atypia, mitoses, and pleomorphism are supportive but not decisive.

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 55-year-old woman undergoes colonoscopy for iron deficiency anemia. A 5 cm ulcerated, firm mass is found in the ascending colon, and biopsy shows irregular malignant glands infiltrating through the muscularis mucosae into the submucosa.
question: This tumor invades locally and has eroded adjacent structures. Which feature of this lesion best explains its difference from a benign colonic adenoma?

options.text: Production of a fibrous capsule that traps the tumor
Uniform, bland nuclei in all tumor cells
Loss of basement membrane integrity with stromal invasion
Slow growth over many years without symptoms
Absence of tumor necrosis in the center of the mass

explanation_correct: Malignant epithelial cells invade the basement membrane using collagenases and hydrolases (metalloproteinases) and lose cell-cell contacts through inactivation of E-cadherin. A benign adenoma remains confined by an intact basement membrane. Destruction of that barrier with extension into the submucosa and beyond is the structural definition of invasive carcinoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: A fibrous capsule would confine the growth and is a feature of benign, well-demarcated lesions rather than of an invasive carcinoma.
explanation_incorrect.B: Uniform bland nuclei indicate a well-differentiated, low-grade lesion and do not explain invasive behavior.
explanation_incorrect.D: Slow growth is typical of benign neoplasms and would not produce local erosion of adjacent structures.
explanation_incorrect.E: Absence of necrosis would suggest a benign or well-differentiated tumor rather than an aggressive, ulcerated carcinoma.

educationalObjective: Invasive carcinoma breaches the basement membrane using metalloproteinases and loses E-cadherin-mediated cell contacts.
source: Generated from 4. Pathology.pdf - Neoplasia: Benign vs malignant characteristics

subject: Pathology
vignette: A 24-year-old woman has a 1.5 cm firm, painless nodule in the thyroid. Fine needle aspiration shows a hypercellular follicular proliferation with a thin, well-defined capsule and no capsular or vascular invasion on the resection specimen.
question: Which of the following is the most important reason this lesion is considered benign?

options.text: The tumor cells are densely cellular
The nodule is larger than 1 cm
There is mild nuclear enlargement
Scattered mitoses are present in the aspirate
There is no capsular or vascular invasion

explanation_correct: Benign tumors stay confined to their site of origin; invasion of the capsule or of vascular channels is a hallmark of malignancy. In follicular thyroid neoplasms the diagnosis of carcinoma rests on identifying capsular or vascular invasion, because cytology alone cannot separate them. Lack of invasion, together with a well-demarcated border, supports a benign follicular adenoma.

explanation_incorrect.A: Dense cellularity is common in both benign adenomas and malignant neoplasms and is not a criterion of benignity.
explanation_incorrect.B: Size alone does not determine benign or malignant behavior; large benign tumors and small carcinomas both occur.
explanation_incorrect.C: Mild nuclear enlargement can occur in benign lesions and in hyperplasia, so it does not establish benign behavior.
explanation_incorrect.D: Scattered mitoses appear in normal proliferative tissue and in benign neoplasms, so they do not exclude malignancy on their own.

educationalObjective: For encapsulated follicular thyroid lesions, the absence of capsular and vascular invasion is what defines a benign adenoma.
